english.title: Political party - make false statement to auditor

additionalkeywords.additionalkeyword: POLITICAL PARTIES ELECTIONS AND REFERENDUMS ACT 2000

english.standardoffencewording:
On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..), knowingly or recklessly made

(A)_[a written]_
(B)_[an oral]_

statement to an auditor, namely **(..SPECIFY NAME..), appointed to carry out an audit under Section 43 of the Political Parties, Elections and Referendums Act 2000, which conveyed or purported to convey information or explanation to which the auditor was entitled by virtue of Section 44(1) of that Act and which was misleading, false or deceptive in a material particular, namely **(..SPECIFY INFORMATION..)
english.legislation: Contrary to section 44(4) of and Schedule 20 to the Political Parties, Elections and Referendums Act 2000.
english.pointstoprove:
date and location
knowingly/recklessly
made a written/oral statement to auditor
which was misleading/false/deceptive

investigatoraction.description: DNA Samples: If crime scene stain present - take evidential sample If no crime scene stain and DNA not confirmed on PNC - take Criminal Justice sample. If DNA confirmed on PNC - CJ sample not required
Confirm proposed charge is appropriately authorised (Police or CPS)
Ensure compliance with investigator's obligations re disclosure
Consider if case suitable for referral to Financial Investigation Unit and CPS for asset recovery eg confiscation order

english.notes:
See Section 84 of the Larceny Act 1861 for "false in
a material particular".

other.penalty:
SUMMARY: Six months imprisonment and / or a fine not exceeding the statutory maximum.
INDICTMENT: One year imprisonment or a fine.

Time limit for prosecutions :
None

On the 12th March 2015 the limit on fines imposed by a Magistrates’ court was removed – as such, the potential fine on summary conviction in relation to an offence committed after this date is unlimited.
